query: For high-entropy alloys intended for demanding engineering applications, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs the retention or loss of toughness, and why? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, the predicted observations relative to a baseline, the boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In single-phase FCC CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys, the retention or loss of toughness is governed primarily by the alloy’s room- and cryogenic-temperature stacking-fault energy (SFE). If the SFE is reduced only slightly (≈ 2–4 mJ m⁻² below the baseline value) deformation twinning is promoted, which raises work-hardening capacity and thus fracture toughness. If the SFE is reduced more strongly (≥ 8 mJ m⁻² below baseline) an fcc → hcp stress-induced martensitic transformation competes with twinning; the resulting hcp laths act as crack-initiation sites and sharply decrease toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy produced by arc-melting, homogenised at 1100 °C for 24 h, water-quenched and cold-rolled 20 %, then recrystallised 1 h at 900 °C to give an average grain size 20–30 µm; no second-phase particles present.
generation.intervention: Isovalent replacement of Ni with Al at 0 at.% (baseline), 1 at.% and 3 at.% Al, all other processing kept identical.
generation.conditions: Charpy V-notch impact and fracture-toughness (J–R curve) tests at 77 K (liquid N2) and 293 K, strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹.
generation.structural_mediator: The equilibrium and deformation-induced faulted structures (intrinsic stacking faults, twin lamellae, hcp martensite plates) that emerge as the SFE is lowered by Al additions.
generation.mechanism: Small Al additions lower SFE moderately, increasing the probability of {111} deformation twinning. Twins act as dynamic Hall–Petch barriers, enhancing strain hardening and delaying necking, which raises energy absorption and toughness. Larger Al additions lower SFE enough that hcp martensite nucleates at intersections of twins and dislocations; the hard, incoherent hcp plates and fcc/hcp interfaces concentrate stress and act as micro-crack embryos, causing premature brittle fracture and loss of toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: 1 at.% Al alloy will show ≥20 % higher Charpy impact energy and a higher J_IC (≈+15–25 %) than the baseline at both 293 K and 77 K; 3 at.% Al alloy will show ≥30 % lower impact energy and J_IC relative to baseline, with fracture surfaces exhibiting hcp laths and cleavage facets.
generation.baseline: Al-free CoCrFeMnNi alloy with SFE ≈ 25 mJ m⁻², showing solely dislocation glide plasticity and moderate toughness (e.g., 150 kJ m⁻² Charpy energy, J_IC ≈ 200 kJ m⁻²).
generation.boundary: Grain size 10–50 µm; single-phase FCC microstructure; test temperatures 77–300 K; Al additions ≤5 at.% and no other strong SFE modifiers present. Outside these ranges, other mechanisms (precipitation, grain-boundary embrittlement, BCC formation) may dominate.
generation.uncertainty: Exact SFE change per at.% Al and the quantitative toughness increments may vary with processing history; unforeseen short-range order or clustering could obscure the simple SFE–toughness correlation.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce the three alloys (0, 1, 3 at.% Al), confirm single-phase FCC by XRD and TEM. Measure SFE by weak-beam TEM or first-principles-aided thermodynamic modelling. Perform instrumented Charpy impact and compact-tension fracture-toughness tests at 77 K and 293 K. Examine post-mortem fracture surfaces and deformation substructures by TEM and EBSD for twins and hcp plates.
measurements: Volume fraction and size of deformation twins (TEM)
Presence and area fraction of hcp martensite (TEM/EBSD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if (a) 1 at.% Al does NOT increase toughness relative to baseline while showing more twins but negligible hcp, or (b) 3 at.% Al does NOT reduce toughness relative to baseline and/or shows no significant increase in hcp martensite fraction.
